claims.text: In 1867 the United States bought Alaska from the Russian Empire.
Canada, Britain and Spain did not sell Alaska; Canada became a dominion only in 1867 and never held Alaska.
The United States paid 7.2 million dollars for Alaska.
Russia sold Alaska partly because it feared it could not defend the colony against Britain.
Critics called the purchase 'Seward's Folly', after Secretary of State William Seward, who negotiated it.
